source_scope: Owned frozen storage extension/engine changes, focused tests and compiled native fixture. Root integration supplies full workspace dependency closure. Public export added in ncollection/mod.rs; rustfmt also reordered existing list_node/node_release module declarations in that touched file.

original_assertion_audit.current_change: No original test body changed. All52 mapped declarations executed on both native and Rust after shared reservation ordering change.

native_fixture.joined_columns: Block count, logical available size, Size, constructor/destructor counts, allocation/free counts, mutable/const raw/typed pointer identities, initialized value, pure round/log results.
native_fixture.allocation_observation: Native derived allocator records allocation/free calls. Rust observes actual live allocations from accumulating_chain at every monotonic allocate-only or free-only stage and accumulates deltas. No expected count is injected, and no phase interleaves hidden allocations and frees.
native_fixture.defined_domain: All block item sizes equal sizeof(Item). Raw pointers are compared only while their allocated storage lives. Only initialized index0 is dereferenced. clearBlocks releases dynamic storage without destructor calls; Item owns no secondary resource and the native container resets Size before its eventual destructor.
native_fixture.numeric_domain: Pure unsigned helper calls include high+1 and SIZE_MAX wrap-to-zero. No overflow-sized array is created or accessed. Fixture recorded on 64-bit native/Rust target.

ownership_and_shared_engine: DynamicArrayStorageExtension owns an exclusive borrow of the array; no block allocation is detached or given another owner.
Const/mutable typed and untyped getters return raw pointers without manufacturing T references to uninitialized capacity. Actual reference access delegates to existing checked value/change_value.

Both existing element-emplacement reservation and new protected reservation now call the shared reserve_block_count method, reserving the pointer vector before block allocations like native ensureBlockCount.
Expansion reuses add_block. clear_blocks reuses the existing forget_block_values_after implementation, then frees blocks and sets logical used size to zero.

Native clearBlocks and Clear(true) intentionally differ: clear_blocks forgets values without Drop, while ordinary clear(true) continues dropping them. Tests observe exact lifetime counts and real allocation release.
safety_boundaries: Block item-size mismatch, zero-sized Rust element types and overflowing logical slot counts are rejected before typed allocation. Native arbitrary-byte allocation signatures remain constrained adapters, not complete raw-domain parity.
Invalid block indices and uninitialized slot access return errors including offending values and expected ranges; native unchecked undefined-access domains are not imitated.
Raw pointer dereference/write requires unsafe caller lifetime, initialization and aliasing guarantees. This batch does not expose setUsedSize or arbitrary lifetime-publication setters.

clear_blocks can intentionally leak secondary resources held by T because native skips destructors; the method documents this explicitly. Forgetting values is safe Rust and no unsafe implementation code was added.
All8 new tests pass MIRIFLAGS=-Zmiri-strict-provenance using the integrated allocator provenance fix. No permissive provenance flag is used.
remaining_partial_parity: Eight protected forms remain outside this batch: allocateBlock, deallocateBlock, setUsedSize, copyParameters, copyDate, constructAt, destroyAt, replaceAt.
The block engine only allocates correctly typed T-sized blocks. Arbitrary raw item sizes and detached allocator/provenance ownership require a separate raw boundary.

Native LinearVector pointer-storage capacity growth and allocation-failure behavior are not fully reproduced by Rust Vec. Verified successful reservation ordering does not prove capacity/OOM-policy parity.
Pure round_up_pow2 matches native defined overflow, but existing constructors still retain their Rust overflow behavior. No invalid overflowing allocation is credited.

Copy partial-block exception cleanup/leak behavior, native custom value move/assignment/destructor dispatch, same-container aliases and cursor behavior remain limited as documented in earlier scoped receipts.
Fourteen declaration-form adapters and sixteen supplemental rows do not establish complete DynamicArray class/template or global API parity.
